title: Babylonian numerals
summary: Rule a square and its diagonals on a round clay tablet, then press the wedge numbers of a Babylonian scribe: one vertical wedge for each unit and a pair of corner wedges for each ten.
howToPlay: The round tablet shows the finished record.
Drag the stylus point along each lit line to rule the square.
Then press at each lit dot and drag a short way toward the point to leave one wedge.
Press Check when every number is written.
rules: Score: how closely your marks sit on the guide. A wedge is made by pressing and dragging a short way; a loose touch leaves only a dimple.
Three stars for 88 or more, two stars for 65 and one star for 40.
Watch and learn plays a whole round for you, and Undo takes back the last step.
heritageNote: Cuneiform means wedge-shaped. Scribes of Mesopotamia pressed a cut reed into soft clay to leave wedge marks, and used place values of sixty. A tablet in the Yale collection shows a square with its diagonals and the number for the square root of two, correct to six figures.
